A1.justification: Both PDFs describe the same MoH research and contain readable main text, equations, tables, figures, and Appendices A–E. Content can be matched across reformatting and renumbering, including the identifiable header error in v2 Table 4.

before.justification: V1 reports original ImageNet classification and generation experiments, language-model training and continue-tuning results, component ablations, and appendix analyses.

after.justification: V2 retains these original experiments and adds inference-time measurements, head-similarity measurements, an activated-head sweep, and routing-score analyses.

M1.justification: Top-K routing, shared heads, two-stage weighting, load-balancing loss, and the LLaMA3 conversion procedure remain unchanged. The sparse-operation description accompanies the new timing experiment; it does not establish a revision to the underlying algorithm.

E1.justification: Both versions use the same ImageNet classification and generation tasks, language-training corpora, and English and Chinese evaluation benchmarks. The new diagnostics and timing measurements change analyses and configurations without adding datasets, domains, or downstream task coverage.

E2.justification: V1 Table 3 includes ADM-G/ADM-U, CDM, LDM-8, LDM-4, and LDM-4-G. These comparators disappear from v2 Table 2, leaving DiT as the only external image-generation comparator and substantially narrowing that comparison. Classification and language-model comparator sets remain unchanged.

E3.justification: V2 adds an attention-timing protocol with 32 heads, head dimension 64, sequence lengths 256 and 512, and sparse matrix multiplication for both methods. It also introduces attention-pattern and output-feature similarity measurements and a 100-epoch activated-head sweep. Existing benchmark training budgets, hyperparameters, and evaluation procedures are retained.

E4.justification: V2 substantially expands the supporting analyses: Table H tests activated-head ratios from 50% to 80%; Table B measures inter-head redundancy; Figures C–E examine shared and routed head scores; and Table 7 tests latency across sequence lengths and activation ratios. The original component ablations, shared-head-ratio study, and head-load visualizations remain.

E5.justification: Neither version reports repeated-run or seed counts, confidence intervals, error bars, or significance tests. V2's additional measurements retain this reporting practice.

E6.justification: Retained benchmark scores are unchanged, but v2 adds substantial new result types. Table 7 reports 0.360 ms for full attention versus 0.225 ms for 50%-active MoH at length 256. Table B reports ViT attention similarity of 0.5159 versus 0.3978. Table H adds 100-epoch accuracies of 78.32% at 50% activation and 78.78% at 80%, while Figures C–E add routing-score findings. The non-DiT generation result rows are removed.

T1.justification: V2 Appendix A.1 and Table A add mathematical expressions comparing gradients over full versus routed data subsets and relating routing weights to effective learning rates. Table B introduces an attention-similarity definition and its bounded range. These are limited mathematical additions, without a new theorem or formal superiority proof.

C1.justification: The central claims remain competitive or superior accuracy using 50%–90% of attention heads and the ability to convert pretrained models into MoH. Both abstracts retain the 64.0% LLaMA3 result and 2.4-point advantage. Shortening the conclusion does not remove claims retained in the abstract and introduction.

C2.justification: V2 adds explanations linking specialization to routed training subsets and adaptive gradient weighting, and explains shared heads' category adaptation through changing routing scores. Section 5 interprets the timing results in relation to routing overhead and sequence length. Existing limitations and the discussion of weaker Chinese and mathematical recovery remain unchanged.

D1.justification: V2 discloses the sparse-matrix implementation used for timing and adds DiT-XL/2 and MoH-DiT-XL/2 parameter counts of 675M and 676M. Existing training settings and sampling ratios are retained, including details moved out of the main text. The supplementary-code and future-cleanup note is removed, while the same repository link remains.

R1.justification: V2 adds a dedicated discussion of attention-head specialization and efficiency, covering Peng et al.'s mixture-of-heads work, SwitchHead, retrieval heads, KV-cache compression, DuoAttention, and vision-head interpretability. The introduction also adds DecAtt and SHViT. This substantially broadens the treatment of closely related research beyond v1's attention, MoE, and MoA discussion.

P1.justification: Most prose and the main section sequence are retained. Changes include localized tightening, reorganized training and evaluation paragraphs, additional appendix subsections, a shorter conclusion, and new acknowledgments and impact statement. These do not amount to extensive rewriting of the existing narrative.

P2.justification: V2 replaces the single-column preprint layout with a two-column conference layout, merges the generation tables, and adds timing, gradient, similarity, activation-sweep, and routing-score displays. Existing figures are relocated, including v1 Figure C becoming v2 Figure F. V2 Table 4 incorrectly repeats the first block's benchmark headers in its second and third blocks, obscuring unchanged scores.

improvement.justification: V2 modestly strengthens support for efficiency and head specialization through direct timing measurements, quantitative redundancy checks, and additional sensitivity analysis, while improving coverage of closely related research. These gains are tempered by the sparse-operator timing setup, which does not establish optimized end-to-end speedups, the removal of non-DiT generation comparisons, and the new benchmark-header errors in Table 4. The central experimental findings remain unchanged.
